newsitem.title: UK: "Neutral" CBI says it could work with UK Labour.
newsitem.headline: "Neutral" CBI says it could work with UK Labour.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry, the UK's main employers' organisation, said on Tuesday it was politically neutral and could work with a Labour government -- as long as economic policy was broadly unchanged.

CBI president Sir Colin Marshall told BBC Radio that industry could work with Labour "so long as the policies adopted by the Labour Party are not at variance with what we believe are the best interests of the country from a business and industry standpoint."

"We are looking at the longest sustained period of economic growth and stability this country has experienced in recent memory. We are the envy of the major countries in Europe," Marshall said, suggesting Labour would be ill-advised to deviate from present economic policies.

As a general rule, British industrialists tend to support the Conservatives. Labour has traditionally been close to the unions, although the ties have been loosened since Tony Blair became leader in 1994.
Labour is well ahead in the opinion polls and looks set to end 18 years of Conservative rule at the next election, which must be held by May, 1997.
Marshall said the CBI as an organisation was politically neutral but its view on economic policy was "to maintain the present position."

He repeated the CBI's opposition to Labour's proposed windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities and its plan to sign up to the Social Chapter of the European Union's Maastricht Treaty, which guarantees minimum working conditions for employees.
